question: A quarry's test chute launches a block of mass 43000 g. The block's speed, in metres per second, is built up as follows: 3 times the sum of the two chute-dial readings, which are 6 and 1, then 13 added, and then 12 subtracted. The chute's guard rail runs 45 m. Twelve identical blocks are launched in a cycle. How much energy does one cycle account for, in J?

A launch site's log gives an energy figure with 6 J added for the igniter and then 1 J subtracted for the timing gate, expressed in kilojoules. That figure covers 9 identical launches, so it is 9 times the energy of a single dart. A dart has a mass of 25000 g. Its launch speed, in metres per second, is 5 times the sum of the two rail-dial settings, which read 3 and 11. What does the log give, in kJ?

A canal lift's regional figure is 4 times a site figure, and a site figure is a paired total less 14 kJ credited back by the counterweight. The paired total is twice the energy of one caisson, since the lift works two caissons. A caisson has a mass of 8000 g on the scale model used for the estimate, and the lift's tower stands 38 m tall. A caisson's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 6 times t. What is the regional figure, in kJ?

A tunnel contractor's site figure is 3 times a heading's force, and each heading works two identical frames, so a heading's force is twice a frame's force. A frame carries 7 identical rams pushing together. One ram drives a mass of 49 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the number of different groups of 4 that can be chosen from the frame's 8 mounting points. The site's ventilation duct is 900 m long. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?

A hydro test rig meters its jet through a run, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 4 times t. The paddle's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second. The paddle has a mass of 28000 g. The rig's sheet takes the paddle's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts 26 kJ drawn by the pump, and then adds back 2 kJ credited to the sensor supply. Eight identical rigs run at the same time, and the site total is 8 times the single-rig figure. What is the site total, in kJ?

A tramway depot tests a car of mass 25000 g on its scale rig. The car's speed, in metres per second, is 4 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 15 times x, plus 56, equals exactly 0. The depot's inspection pit is 18 m long. The depot's sheet takes the car's kinetic energy in kilojoules and adds 22 kJ drawn by the substation. Ten identical cars run on the line, and the report gives 10 times the single-car figure. What does the report give, in kJ?

A shipyard's site figure is a yard total less 1 kN allowed for the tie-down bolts. The yard total is 5 times a bay's force, and each bay carries 7 identical hoists, so a bay's force is 7 times one hoist's force in kilonewtons. One hoist drives a load of mass 74 kg. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the hoist's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 1st second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 7 times t. What is the shipyard's site figure, in kN?

A cable-tension rig's report is a bank total less 13 kN for the frame's own reaction. The bank total is 11 times a single actuator's corrected force, and an actuator's corrected force is the force on its load in kilonewtons plus 5 kN for the anchor plate. The load has a mass of 49000 g. Its speed along the guide, in metres per second, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 0 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the rig takes how fast that speed is changing at the instant 3 seconds in as the load's acceleration. What does the rig's report give, in kN?

A gantry crane test rig drives a block of mass 76000 g. The block's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the rig's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 3 times t. Ten identical blocks hang from each gantry, and the yard operates 11 gantries. The yard's sheet then subtracts 22 kN allowed for the rail restraint. What does the yard's sheet give, in kN?

A workshop's hall figure is 7 times a bench's balance, because seven identical benches run together. A bench's balance is the driving force in kilonewtons, less 15 kN allowed for the granite base and then plus 25 kN for the tie-down frame. The driven slide has a mass of 62000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, equals exactly 0. What is the workshop's hall figure, in kN?

A test bench's final entry takes an energy figure, subtracts 9 J for the release catch, adds 17 J credited to the sensor supply, and then subtracts 19 J for the brake. That energy figure is the kinetic energy of a puck of mass 23 kg. The puck's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the bench's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second. The meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 2 times t. What is the bench's final entry, in J?

A mine hoist's total is 8 times a shaft figure, and each shaft figure is 8 times the force on a single skip, because eight skips hang on every rope set. A skip has a mass of 46 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 9 times a number x, with 1 then added. That number x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 7 times x, plus 6, equals exactly 0. What is the mine hoist's total, in N?

A bridge-jacking contractor's site figure is 11 times a pier's balance. A pier's balance is the jacking force in kilonewtons, plus 21 kN for the packing plates and then less 10 kN credited to the bearing shims. The jack drives a mass of 196000 g. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together the squares of each whole number from 1 to 4. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?

A conveyor works drives a pallet of mass 140000 g. The pallet's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 6, equals exactly 0. Five identical pallets run on each lane, and the lane log then adds 20 N for the belt drag. Three lanes make up a bank, and the works runs 6 identical banks. What total force do the works' drives supply, in N?

A depot's balance is a paired figure in kilojoules, less 13 kJ drawn by the compressor. The paired figure is twice the energy of a single trolley, since the trolleys always run in pairs. A trolley has a mass of 54000 g, and the depot's inspection lamp draws 70 W. A trolley's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 364 and 295 exactly. What does the depot's balance give, in kJ?

A quayside crane meters its hoist through a lift, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 7 times t. The crane takes the total accumulated between the 1st and the 3rd second and subtracts 17 to obtain the load's acceleration in metres per second squared. The load has a mass of 66 kg, and the crane's jib reaches 30 m. The log adds 22 N for the sheave friction, and the quay works two identical cranes on the same lift, doubling the figure. What does the log record, in kN?

A dry-dock operator's yard figure is 12 times a single caisson's balance, expressed in kilonewtons. A caisson's balance is the driving force plus 13 kN for the seal ring and then a further 18 kN for the guide shoes. The caisson has a mass of 170 kg on the scale rig used for the estimate. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the rig's meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 5 times t. What is the operator's yard figure, in kN?

A pumping station's plant figure is a hall force in kilonewtons plus 11 kN for the base slab. The hall force covers 12 identical banks, and each bank has 8 identical rams pushing together. One ram drives a mass of 46 kg. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 12 times the value, plus 32, equals exactly 0. The station's outfall pipe is 300 m long. What is the plant figure, in kN?

A rail depot's shed figure is 11 times the force taken by a single bay, expressed in kilonewtons. A bay drives a wagon of mass 173 kg. The wagon's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is a meter total minus 5. That total is what the bay's meter accumulates between the 1st and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 3 times t. The depot's inspection pit is 30 m long. What is the shed figure, in kN?

A dockside conveyor's site figure is twice a bay total, because two identical bays run at the same time. A bay total is 5 times a single sack's booked energy, expressed in kilojoules. A sack's booked energy is its kinetic energy less 7 J absorbed by the chute liner. The sack has a mass of 56000 g, and its speed, in metres per second, equals the total the chute meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 1 times t. What is the site figure, in kJ?

A quarry's shift figure is 11 times a net cycle figure, expressed in kilojoules. A net cycle figure is the combined energy of 6 identical skips, less 21 J absorbed by the tipping latch. A skip has a mass of 46000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 13 times the value, plus 42, equals exactly 0. What is the quarry's shift figure, in kJ?

A hydro test flume meters its gate through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 3 times t squared plus 3 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, is the total accumulated between the 1st and the 3rd second, plus 20. The float has a mass of 55 kg. The run sheet takes the float's kinetic energy and adds 19 J drawn by the gate motor. Four identical flumes run together, and the site log then subtracts 19 J credited back by the recovery turbine. What does the site log record, in J?

A wave-tank rig meters its paddle through a stroke, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 5 times t squared plus 6 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, equals the total accumulated between the 0th and the 1st second. The float has a mass of 18000 g, and the rig's control lamp draws 45 W. The run sheet takes the float's kinetic energy and subtracts 11 J drawn by the paddle motor, and the rig runs a mirrored second tank, doubling the figure. What does the run sheet give, in kJ?

A brick works drives a ram carrying a mass of 98 kg. The ram's position along its guide, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 0 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the works takes how fast it is moving at the instant 1 second in as the acceleration in metres per second squared. Seven identical rams work each press, and the press log then adds 14 N for the ejector spring. The works operates 6 identical presses. What total force do the works' presses supply, in N?

A dry dock's gate rig drives a caisson of mass 192 kg on its scale model. The caisson's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 3 times t. The rig's log subtracts 12 N for the seal drag. Expressed in kilonewtons, the yard sheet then adds 10 kN for the sill anchors. The yard operates 5 identical gates, and its report gives 5 times the single-gate figure. What does the report give, in kN?
